time.desc: Foreign media claimed that indirect talks between the two countries originally scheduled to be held under the mediation of a third party were temporarily canceled, and negotiations on ceasefire and nuclear-related issues suffered a setback.

One side issued the latest safety and traffic guidelines for ships passing through key sea lanes and continued to implement port blockades, while the highest level issued a signal that "dialogue may be resumed."
The leader of one party publicly listed "facilitating regime change" as a foreign policy goal on social platforms, and the other party immediately warned of counterattacks in tough terms.

Indirect negotiations at the technical level between the two sides were officially launched in a third place. At the same time, one side held live-fire drills near key sea lanes and briefly announced restrictions on passage to demonstrate deterrence.
The mediator publicly stated that an agreement between the two countries was close to being reached, signaling that the negotiations were "final".

The two sides launched large-scale joint air strikes against each other, escalating the confrontation into an open war, and the major result of the death of the other side's top leadership in the first round of strikes was confirmed to the outside world.

For the first time, one party participating in the war publicly confirmed that its combatants were killed, which was caused by the opponent's drone/missile counterattack against its overseas support nodes.

The belligerent countries confirmed the completion of the transfer of supreme power during the war, and relatives of the original supreme leader succeeded to core positions without going through elections.

Senior officials from one of the parties to the war publicly stated that they had "no objection" to the passage of ships from some countries in key sea lanes, and linked future energy market intervention to the duration of the conflict.

The coalition launched a new round of air strikes on the opponent's important energy infrastructure and triggered fluctuations in international energy prices. At the same time, its leader said that the war will "end soon."

The leaders of one of the parties involved in the war issued a time-limited ultimatum to their opponents, demanding that commercial shipping in key sea lanes be restored, otherwise the opponent's key livelihood infrastructure such as electricity will be hit.

The military statements of the belligerent countries stated that if the other party fulfills its threat to attack energy facilities, it will take escalating countermeasures such as "comprehensive closure of key sea lanes."

One of the parties involved in the war announced that it had opened dialogue with its opponent and promised to suspend attacks on the opponent's energy facilities in the short term in exchange for a window for negotiation.
One party participating in the war formally submitted an armistice plan containing multiple clauses to its opponent in an attempt to promote framework negotiations to end the conflict.
The belligerents completed formal replies to the armistice terms proposed by the other party, bringing the ceasefire negotiations into a new stage.

The two countries outside the region jointly proposed another set of multi-point initiatives for "immediate ceasefire and restoration of normal traffic in key sea lanes", forming a mediation path parallel to the warring parties' plans.

In a nationally televised address, leaders of one side of the war announced tougher attacks on their opponents in the coming weeks and once again gave a timetable for trying to end the conflict within weeks.
